title: Dualizing composition mate and normalization of transposed exchange
statement:
Fix primes $p\ne\ell$, $a\ge1$, $q=p^a$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, an algebraic closure $k$ of $k_0$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in a fixed algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, and $\Lambda\in\{E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Let $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ be a separated finite-type morphism between separated finite-type $k_0$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], with geometric fiber $f:X\to Y$. For $T=X,Y$ put $\Phi_T=Lg_T^*$ for geometric Frobenius $g_T$ [def-weil-frobenius-detailed, def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Work in the rational/common-stage bounded constructible categories with Weil pairs $(K,\theta_K:\Phi_TK\xrightarrow{\sim}K)$ and arrows $u\theta_K=\theta_L\Phi_T(u)$ [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. Set $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $a_T:T\to s$, $\omega_T=Ra_T^!\Lambda_s$, $D_T=R\mathcal Hom_T(-,\omega_T)$, using the constructible exceptional adjoints [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. Write $F=Rf_!$, $G=Rf^!$, $P=Lf^*$ and $Q=Rf_*$. All objects, functors, adjunctions and composites below are restricted to a supplied domain on which they exist; no ambient exceptional right adjoint is assumed.

Use the canonical Weil lifts of the operations and adjunctions, with equivariant units, counits, tensor evaluation, and the compact-support compositor. Put $H=Ra_Y{}_!$, $J=Ra_Y^!$, $U=Ra_X{}_!$, $W=Ra_X^!$, and let $\alpha:HF\xrightarrow{\sim}U$ be that compositor for $a_X=a_Yf$. Use the pasted adjunction $HF\dashv GJ$ and the adjunction $U\dashv W$, with $\eta^U$ the latter's unit. For every object $Z$ in their common domain put
$$\varepsilon^{HF}_Z=\varepsilon^H_Z\circ H(\varepsilon^F_{JZ}),\qquad c_Z=W(\varepsilon^{HF}_Z\circ\alpha^{-1}_{GJZ})\circ\eta^U_{GJZ}:GJZ\to WZ.$$
This is the specified right-adjoint composition isomorphism: the mate of $\alpha^{-1}$ under these adjunctions, in the convention of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. Each $c_Z$ is a Weil morphism when $Z$ is a Weil object. At the coefficient unit $Z=\Lambda_s$ it is the canonical $c:G\omega_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_X$, with no independent choice of dualizing identification.

For a Weil object $M$ on $X$, set $H_M=R\mathcal Hom_X(M,-)$, $A=D_YFM$, and $V=M\otimes^LPA$. Suppose the projection map $\pi:FM\otimes^LA\xrightarrow{\sim}FV$ of [def-exchange-projection] is defined and invertible. Let $b=\operatorname{ev}_{FM}\pi^{-1}$ and let $t:V\to G\omega_Y$ be its exceptional transpose. Denote tensor--Hom and ordinary adjunction transposition by $(-)^{\sharp_\otimes}$ and $(-)^{\sharp_*}$. The following equality holds in the derived category:
$$\bigl((c\circ t)^{\sharp_\otimes}\bigr)^{\sharp_*}
=QH_M(c)\circ\bigl(t^{\sharp_\otimes}\bigr)^{\sharp_*}:A\to QD_XM.$$
In particular the right side is exactly the canonical component $\epsilon_M$ of [def-sf-verdier-exchange-data], which substitutes $c$ before those last two transposes. The substitution map $QH_M(c)$ is a Weil morphism for the supplied lifted functors. When $f,a_X,a_Y$ and $M$ satisfy all the exceptional-admissibility and finite-Tor hypotheses of [fix-lem-tensor-adjunction, fix-cor-verdier-exchange], let
$$I_{M,\omega_Y}:QH_M(G\omega_Y)\xrightarrow{\sim}D_YFM$$
be the internal-adjunction isomorphism of [fix-lem-tensor-adjunction] at $N=\omega_Y$, in the following normalization: for every $B\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$ and every $u:B\to QH_M(G\omega_Y)$, the arrow $I_{M,\omega_Y}\circ u:B\to D_YFM$ is the image of $u$ under the composite of the natural bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}(B,QH_M(G\omega_Y))\cong\operatorname{Hom}(PB,H_M(G\omega_Y))\cong\operatorname{Hom}(M\otimes^LPB,G\omega_Y)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(F(M\otimes^LPB),\omega_Y)\xrightarrow{-\circ\pi_{M,B}}\operatorname{Hom}(FM\otimes^LB,\omega_Y)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(B,D_YFM),$$
given successively by the adjunctions $P\dashv Q$, $M\otimes^L-\dashv H_M$ and $F\dashv G$, precomposition with the projection map $\pi_{M,B}:FM\otimes^LB\to F(M\otimes^LPB)$ of [def-exchange-projection], and the tensor--Hom adjunction $FM\otimes^L-\dashv R\mathcal Hom_Y(FM,-)$ with counit evaluation. Then $\bigl(t^{\sharp_\otimes}\bigr)^{\sharp_*}$ is an isomorphism and
$$\bigl(t^{\sharp_\otimes}\bigr)^{\sharp_*}=I_{M,\omega_Y}^{-1},\qquad
\epsilon_M=QH_M(c)\circ I_{M,\omega_Y}^{-1}.$$
Thus the stage-conclusion isomorphism of [fix-cor-verdier-exchange] has this precise component. The identities fix the projection map, the composition mate and the order of the transposes, at rational coefficients and in the common-stage category. Only the invertibility and the last two identities involving $I$ invoke the additional admissibility and finite-Tor hypotheses; the mate and substitution identity hold on every supplied domain where their displayed data exist.

proof.text: Expand VerdierExchange.composition using Mathlib conjugateIsoEquiv_apply_hom and conjugateEquiv_apply_app, and expand the pasted counit using Adjunction.comp_counit_app. This is the displayed formula. Derive the underlying inverse compositor equation from alphaW.inv_hom_id_app and the supplied underlying hom equation by cancellation of alpha.hom. Expand the same formula in IsoAlgebra; forgetful composition and map equations, together with the supplied unit_eq and counit_eq fields, identify its underlying arrow with the ordinary mate.

The construction weilComposition is a natural isomorphism in the category IsoAlgebra of fixed pairs, so its components are already equivariant arrows. The underlying-arrow equality in Step 1 identifies these components with the displayed composition mate, including at the coefficient unit.

proof.text: Unfold lastTransposes. Apply ax.homEquiv_naturality_right to transpose postcomposition by c through tensor--Hom. This gives the tensor transpose of t followed by H_M(c), on any supplied domain.

source.place: Sentence 4: substitution through tensor--Hom transposition; expanded directly from its unit formula.

proof.text: Apply o.adj.homEquiv_naturality_right to the result of Step 3. The resulting equation is precisely substitution: lastTransposes(t followed by c) equals lastTransposes(t) followed by QH_M(c).

source.place: Sentence 4: substitution through ordinary adjunction transposition; expanded directly from its unit formula.

proof.text: The definition exchangeComponent substitutes c before lastTransposes, whereas preExchange omits that substitution, so Step 4 gives the first component identity directly. For substitution_weil, apply the recorded Hom lift to c and then the recorded right-adjoint lift. The algebra-morphism equation of this composite lifted arrow, reversed, is the required structure equation.

source.place: Sentence 4: identify the specified exchange component; fix-cor-verdier-exchange.proof.md Step 2.

proof.text: Use the normalized isomorphism I supplied in the conditional hypothesis; its existence is not asserted or needed here. Set A to the Hom object on Y. The two HEq projection normalizations imply piAll A = pi.hom. Apply the stipulated Hom-chain equation to preExchange. Unfold the chain and the three transposes; cancel each adjunction equivalence against its inverse. Replace piAll A by pi.hom, cancel pi.hom followed by pi.inv, and use homEquiv_symm_id to identify the tensor transpose of the counit with the identity. Thus preExchange followed by I.hom is the identity. Cancel I.hom to obtain preExchange = I.inv; transfer IsIso from I.inv and substitute this equality in Step 4. All test objects already lie in the supplied category; no separate finite-Tor theorem or construction of I is used.

proof.text: For stage_epsilon, unfold StageData.epsilon, stageTensorModel, Model.inverseComponent and CoefficientClosedStructure.transpose. Apply homEquiv_naturality_right first for closedX.adjunction M and then for the ordinary adjunction. The underlying Hom functor map is definitionally homX.map (Prod.mkHom (identity (op M)) dualizing.hom), giving the specified substitution formula. Compose with StageConclusion.components to get the same formula for every supplied stage conclusion.
